title: USS Theodore Roosevelt Arrives in the Middle East as a Third US Carrier, Yemeni Forces Pull Back From Bab al-Mandab to Defend Aden, and a ULA Vulcan Rocket Fails on Launch
subhead: The USS Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group arrived in the Middle East to give US Central Command three aircraft carriers in the theater as Iranian drones targeted a US base in Bahrain; Yemeni government troops withdrew from positions near the Bab al-Mandab Strait to defend Aden against a Houthi offensive; and a United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket exploded after liftoff from Florida.

sections.heading: USS Theodore Roosevelt Arrives in the Middle East as a Third US Carrier While Iran Targets a Bahrain Base
sections.body:
Al Jazeera, Times of Israel, and USNI News — The aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) and its embarked Carrier Air Wing 11 arrived in the Middle East following their transit from Singapore, bringing the total number of US Navy carrier strike groups operating in the region to three as Tehran warned it could strike first rather than wait for an American or Israeli offensive. Bloomberg reported Monday that Iranian kamikaze drones targeted a US military base in Bahrain—triggering civil defense sirens across the kingdom—even as Iranian officials signaled that diplomatic channels for a US ceasefire agreement remain open. Along Iran's western border, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps stated it neutralized an armed PKK-linked PJAK cell planning cross-border attacks (Anadolu Agency).

In Washington, scrutiny of the Pentagon's handling of the eight-month conflict intensified as The Atlantic reported that senior defense officials had ignored earlier intelligence warnings detailing the operational threat of Iran's long-range one-way attack drones, while CBS News's 60 Minutes broadcast interviews with Gold Star families of US service members killed in the Iran war demanding answers from Pentagon leadership.
sections.whyItMatters: Concentrating three US carrier strike groups in the Middle East while Iranian drones target air defenses in Bahrain underscores the high risk of miscalculation even as Washington and Tehran explore ceasefire terms.

sections.heading: Yemeni Government Forces Pull Back From Bab al-Mandab to Defend Aden as Houthis Strike an Aden Military Camp
sections.body:
Al Jazeera and Anadolu Agency — Yemeni government military units announced a tactical withdrawal from positions near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait and regrouped around Taiz to reinforce the perimeter of the interim capital Aden against advancing Houthi forces. As fighting escalated along the southern approaches, Houthi missile units launched ballistic missiles at the al-Qawa military camp inside Aden and claimed long-range drone and missile strikes against military and oil targets in Riyadh.

Elsewhere in the Middle East theater, Palestinian medical officials reported that three Palestinians were killed in Israeli drone strikes across Gaza, including two near a mosque northwest of Rafah (Anadolu Agency), while Israeli troops injured two Palestinians in the occupied West Bank (Anadolu Agency). Inside Israel, prime minister-designate Gadi Eisenkot—a former IDF chief of staff whose military background is shaping his coalition strategy (Breaking Defense)—warned that fair elections cannot be held while Benjamin Netanyahu remains in office, even as 15 detained Haredi draft evaders were celebrated and awarded 147,000 shekels at a ceremony in Bnei Brak (Times of Israel).
sections.whyItMatters: A Houthi push that forces Yemeni government troops away from the Bab al-Mandab coastline strengthens Houthi control over the southern Red Sea maritime corridor.

sections.heading: A ULA Vulcan Rocket Explodes After Florida Liftoff as the Pentagon Rebrands Its Principal AI Office
sections.body:
Ars Technica, South China Morning Post, and Breaking Defense — United Launch Alliance suffered the first total mission failure in its 20-year history on Sunday when its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed shortly after liftoff from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, destroying a payload of 40 broadband satellites for Amazon's Leo constellation. The launch failure deals a significant operational setback to ULA—a joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin—which serves alongside SpaceX as a primary heavy-lift launch provider for US National Security Space Launch intelligence and military reconnaissance payloads.

Inside the Pentagon, Breaking Defense reported that the Defense Department formally rebranded its principal artificial intelligence directorate as the 'Super Intelligence Office' in compliance with President Donald Trump's government-wide directive to replace AI terminology. Meanwhile, the Washington Post reported that Pentagon legal authorities are preparing a military court-martial prosecution of a general officer accused of leaking classified defense information, while at the United Nations in Geneva and New York diplomats prepared to debate binding international rules on lethal autonomous weapons systems (AFP).
sections.whyItMatters: The Vulcan Centaur failure will trigger an anomaly investigation that could delay upcoming US Space Force national security satellite launches.

sections.heading: US, Japan, Australia, and the Philippines Build a Four-Nation South China Sea Defense Hub as China Pairs the J-10C With a Heavy Missile
sections.body:
South China Morning Post, USNI News, and The War Zone — The United States, Japan, Australia, and the Philippines are accelerating the creation of a four-country operational defense coordination center to counter Chinese maritime coercion in the South China Sea, the South China Morning Post reported Monday. The quadrilateral initiative builds on Tokyo's agreement last week to transfer coastal defense radars and surveillance drones to the Armed Forces of the Philippines and Washington's delivery of two T38 Devil Ray unmanned surface vessels to the Philippine Marine Corps at Subic Bay (USNI News).

Across the Taiwan Strait, new imagery analyzed by the South China Morning Post showed a Chinese People's Liberation Army Air Force J-10C multirole fighter carrying a modified Russian-origin heavy-strike missile, while Interesting Engineering examined how China's mobile HQ-17A short-range air-defense network is designed to shield amphibious forces near the strait. Reflecting on the approaching 2027 milestone, former US Indo-Pacific Command chief Adm. Philip Davidson told The War Zone that he hopes his famous 'Davidson Window' assessment of Beijing's readiness to invade Taiwan by 2027 proves wrong.
sections.whyItMatters: Integrating US, Japanese, Australian, and Philippine command networks creates a standing coalition posture in the South China Sea just as PLA air and coastal missile capabilities expand.

sections.heading: Pentagon Stalls Ukraine's Patriot Missile Production License as the US Army Names an Officer Held in a UK Espionage Probe
sections.body:
Defense News and USNI News — The Pentagon has stalled Ukraine's request for an industrial license to domestically manufacture Patriot air-defense interceptor missiles, Euromaidan Press reported, slowing Kyiv's push to build local munition reserves against Russian ballistic missile strikes. In the United Kingdom, the US Army officially identified Lt. Col. Brandon Carroll Tyner as the American officer arrested by British authorities earlier in the week on allegations of espionage for Russian intelligence (Defense News), while the International Criminal Court closed the portion of its Afghanistan war-crimes investigation that could have scrutinized US personnel to focus exclusively on the Taliban (Defense News).

In allied force modernization, newly released budget documents showed Italy increased its spending on the sixth-generation Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP) fighter while trimming funding for new army tanks and armored vehicles (Defense News). Meanwhile, Defense News highlighted expanding talks between Turkey and Egypt on joint naval warship construction, and USNI News reported that the British Type-31 Arrowhead design is among the six international contenders shortlisted for the US Navy's next-generation frigate program.
sections.whyItMatters: Withholding a local Patriot production license limits Ukraine's long-term air-defense autonomy at a delicate moment in ceasefire diplomacy.

bottomLine: Monday's defense landscape reflects mounting operational strain across three theaters at once: the arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt gives the US three carriers in the Middle East as Houthi forces push toward Aden and Iranian drones hit Bahrain, ULA's first-ever total launch failure on the Vulcan Centaur complicates US military space access, and the Pentagon's hold on Ukraine's Patriot production license alongside a four-nation South China Sea defense center shows Washington rationing industrial support in Europe while reinforcing the Indo-Pacific.
